SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p165/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p165/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p165/r2.claim: Al-Mu’minun describes faith generally, while al-Ma‘arij specifies belief in Judgment; the former is more comprehensive and thus fuller.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p165/r2.anchor: فذكر صفة الإيمان على وجه العموم. وقال في آية (المعارج)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p165/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p165/r3.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p165/r3.claim: Rūḥ al-Ma‘ānī reports a view that believers here affirm the Prophet’s religious essentials, including monotheism, prophethood, bodily resurrection, and recompense.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p165/r3.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) في قوله: {قد أفلح المؤمنون} "والمراد بالمؤمنين قيل:

DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.claim: Aflaha can mean becoming happy or blessed.
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.anchor: افلح سعد قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمنين قد افلح المؤمنون يعني سعدوا وقال تعالى في سورة سبح قد افلح من تزكى

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r3.claim: This exchange may also be described as inheritance, as explained under the opening of al-Mu’minun.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r3.anchor: وقد يخبر عن هذا التبادل بالوراثة كما بيناه في قد أفلح المؤمنون

ASAD-NOTES:23:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:intro/r1.speaker: classical commentators; Suyuti
ASAD-NOTES:23:intro/r1.claim: Most classical commentators date the surah late in the Meccan period; some call it the final Meccan revelation, though Asad finds no conclusive evidence.
ASAD-NOTES:23:intro/r1.anchor: we have no conclusive evidence to that effect

ASAD-NOTES:23:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:intro/r3.claim: Its central argument is that belief in God as a conscious Creator logically requires belief in life after death.
ASAD-NOTES:23:intro/r3.anchor: it is logically impossible to believe in God as a conscious Creative Power without believing in the reality of a life after death as well

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r1.speaker: Q

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.claim: The surah opens by describing the virtues and righteous actions of believers.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.anchor: begins by describing the virtues and righteous actions of those who believe

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r1.claim: Al-Mu’minūn is the counterpart and supplement of al-Ḥajj: the previous sūrah ends with the community's duty to witness the true religion, and this sūrah begins on the same subject, with its opening and closing verses interlocking.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r2.claim: The sūrahs share themes but differ in style and reasoning: al-Ḥajj announces believers' success and disbelievers' disgrace, while al-Mu’minūn details believers' traits and the certainty of disbelievers' humiliation; temporary trials and respite end when truth triumphs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r2.anchor: Ultimately, the truth will triumph and evil will be routed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r3.claim: Verses 1–11 promise believers success and Paradise subject to stated conditions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p236/r3.anchor: Believers are given glad tidings of success and entry into Paradise

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p238/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p238/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p238/r1.claim: The foremost referent of believers is the brave Meccan emigrants preparing for jihad; past-tense success expresses certainty, principally the Hereafter, while also subsuming the promised establishment of God's religion in Arabia and other gains under Paradise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p238/r1.anchor: The glad tidings of success sounded in this verse relate to the future but they are expressed in the past tense.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p286/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p286/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p286/r1.claim: The sūrah's ending contrasts its opening: believers are declared successful at the start, while disbelievers are said never to succeed at the end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p286/r1.anchor: The sūrah began with the words “Those believers succeeded who …” and is ending on the words “the disbelievers shall never succeed.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.claim: Al-Mu'minūn's opening describes success through humble prayer, avoiding frivolity, zakāh, chastity and restraint, trustworthiness, and keeping promises.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.anchor: salvation and success before God is reserved for those believers whose prayers are marked with humility and concentration

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r6.claim: This surah is Meccan, without disagreement.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r7.speaker: الحاكم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r7.claim: In al-Hakim's Sahih, the Prophet says that whoever upholds the ten verses beginning قد أفلح المؤمنون will enter Paradise, then recites them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r7.anchor: وفي الصحيح للحاكم عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «لقد أنزلت علي عشر آيات من أقامهن دخل الجنة»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r8.claim: The surah's opening follows the previous surah's address to believers to bow and hope for success: this opening announces that the hoped-for success has been attained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r8.anchor: ومناسبتها لآخر السورة قبلها ظاهرة لأنه تعالى خاطب المؤمنين بقوله يا أيها الذين آمنوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r9.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف وعمرو بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r9.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif and Amr ibn Ubayd read قد أفلح المؤمنون in a passive form, meaning they have been brought into success; this may derive from intransitive فلح or transitive or intransitive أفلح.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r9.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف وعمرو بن عبيد قد أفلح المؤمنون بضم الهمزة وكسر اللام مبنيا للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r10.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r10.claim: Talha also has a reading with fatḥa on hamza and lām and ḍamma on ḥāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p545/r10.anchor: وقرأ طلحة أيضا بفتح الهمزة واللام وضم الحاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r1.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r1.claim: Isa ibn Umar says he heard Talha read قد أفلحوا المؤمنون and challenged him as making a grammatical error; Talha replied that he was following the same error as his companions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r1.anchor: سمعت طلحة بن مصرف يقرأ قد أفلحوا المؤمنون، فقلت له: أتلحن؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r2.claim: The author explains Talha's reply as referring to transmitted readings, not an actual solecism: the form follows the dialect exemplified by أكلوني البراغيث.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r2.anchor: يعني أن مرجوعه في القراءة إلى ما روي وليس بلحن لأنه على لغة أكلوني البراغيث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers another analysis as an ambiguous expression followed by an explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أو على الإبهام والتفسير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls this reading rejected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وهي قراءة مردودة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r5.claim: Ibn Khalawayh's book writes a wāw after ḥāʾ; al-Lawamiʿ says the plural wāw is omitted in connected speech when it meets the following wāw, and the spelling reflects connected pronunciation, as in ويمح الله الباطل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r5.anchor: وفي كتاب ابن خالويه مكتوبا بواو بعد الحاء، وفي اللوامح وحذفت واو الجمع بعد الحاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports from Talha أفلح with a ḍamma and no wāw, treating the vowel as sufficient in place of it, and cites a line of poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r6.anchor: وعنه أي عن طلحة أفلح بضمة بغير واو اجتزاء بها عنها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r7.claim: The author rejects the comparison: the wāw in أفلحوا is omitted to avoid two still letters, whereas the omitted wāw in the other form is due to poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r7.anchor: وليس بجيد لأن الواو في أفلح حذفت لالتقاء الساكنين وهنا حذفت للضرورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says قد with the past verb asserts an expected result; the believers expected this glad tidings, so its form affirms the lasting success they anticipated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r8.anchor: قد تقتضيه لما هي تثبت المتوقع ولما تنفيه

SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r1.claim: The general reading has أفلح as an active past verb with open hamza and ḥā.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r1.anchor: العامة على " أفلح " مفتوح الهمزة والحاء فعلا ماضيا مبنيا للفاعل.

SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r2.speaker: ورش
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r2.claim: Warsh applies his established rule of moving the hamza vowel to the preceding still consonant and deleting the hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r2.anchor: وورش على قاعدته من نقل حركة الهمزة إلى الساكن قبلها وحذفها.

SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r3.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r3.claim: Hamza has two reported pause forms: one like Warsh and another like the general reading.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r3.anchor: وعن حمزة في الوقف خلف: فروي عنه كورش، وكالجماعة.

SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa explains hamza transfer by turning the hamza into alif and deleting it at the original meeting of two vowelless letters; the author objects that this assumes a weaker dialect and an unnecessary underlying cause.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r4.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " من ألقى حركة الهمزة على الدال وحذفها فعلته: أن الهمزة بعد حذف حركتها صيرت ألفا،

SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r5.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف وعمرو بن عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r5.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif and Amr ibn Ubayd read أفلح in the passive, meaning they entered into felicity; the author notes that أفلح can also mean to bring someone into felicity.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r5.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف وعمرو بن عبيد " أفلح " مبنيا للمفعول أي: دخلوا في الفلاح.

SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r6.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r6.claim: Talha also reads أفلح with open hamza and lām and ḍamma on ḥā, using a plural marker before the subject like أكلوني البراغيث.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r6.anchor: وقرأ طلحة أيضا " أفلح " بفتح الهمزة واللام وضم الحاء. وتخريجها على أن الأصل

SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r7.speaker: عيسى
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r7.claim: Isa reports that when he asked Talha if this was a grammatical error, Talha replied that he read it as his companions had erred, meaning he faithfully followed their transmitted reading.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r7.anchor: قال عيسى: " سمعت طلحة يقرؤها. فقلت له: أتلحن؟ قال: نعم كما لحن أصحابي "

SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls Talha's plural-marker reading rejected; the author objects that analogous constructions occur in two unanimously accepted Quranic readings.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " وهي قراءة مردودة ". قلت: ولا أدري كيف يردونها مع ثبوت مثلها

SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports from Talha a form with ḍamma on ḥā but no wāw, treating the vowel as a substitute for it; the author finds the comparison with the cited poem inexact.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " وعنه أي عن طلحة " أفلح " بضمة بغير واو، اجتزاء بها عنها كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r1.claim: The missing wāw is necessary in connected speech to prevent two vowelless sounds from meeting, while its omission in the poem is poetic license, so the cases do not match.

SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r2.speaker: ابن خالويه
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r2.claim: Ibn Khalawayh's book writes a wāw after the ḥā in Talha's reading.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r2.anchor: ففي كتاب ابن خالويه مكتوبا بواو بعد الحاء،

SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r3.speaker: اللوامح
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r3.claim: Al-Lawami says the wāw is deleted in connected recitation and writing follows connection, with examples from other verses.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r3.anchor: وفي " اللوامح ": " وحذفت الواو بعد الحاء لالتقائهما في الدرج، وكانت الكتابة عليها محمولة على الوصل

SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes قد here as marking expectation, the opposite of لما, which denies what is expected; it assures believers that their anticipated success will endure.

SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says believers expected this good news, so قد speaks to them in a form confirming the lasting success they anticipated.
SAMIN-DURR:23:1#2/r5.anchor: ولا شك أن المؤمنين كانوا متوقعين لهذه البشارة، وهي للإخبار بثبات الفلاح لهم

ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r1.anchor: ومن السورة التي يذكر فيها المؤمنون. قوله تعالى:

ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r2.claim: The believers have attained lasting continuance in goodness; an alternate reading means they were brought to success.
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r2.anchor: أي قد نالوا البقاء الدائم في الخير، ومن قرأ قد أفلح المؤمنون.

ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r3.speaker: كعب الحبر
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r3.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār reports that God created Adam, the Garden of Eden, and the Torah with His hand; when told to speak, Eden said قد أفلح المؤمنون on seeing its inhabitants' honors.
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r3.anchor: ويروى عن كعب الحبر: أن الله عز وجل لم يخلق بيده إلا ثلاثة أشياء، خلق آدم

ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r4.claim: Believers affirm what came from God, His oneness without partner, and that Muhammad is His prophet.
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r4.anchor: و (المؤمنون) المصدقون بما أتى من عند الله، وبأنه واحد لا شريك له.

ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.claim: Believers attain a happy state through humility in prayer and active pursuit of inner purity.
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.anchor: TRULY, to a happy state shall attain the believe rs: (23:2) those who humble themselves

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r1.claim: The Qur’an associates believers’ khushūʿ with worship in worldly life, citing the believers’ prayer, the faithful People of the Book, and earlier prophets.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r1.anchor: آل عمران 199: {خَاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ لَا يَشْتَرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا}

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r2.claim: When criminals, disbelievers, or wrongdoers are described as humble, the context is the afterlife and the humiliation of judgment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r2.anchor: فإذا جاء الخشوع، في البيان القرآني من المجرمين والكفار، فذلك إنما يكون منهم في اليوم الآخر الذي كانوا يوعدون

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r3.claim: She highlights the rhetorical contrast: believers show khushūʿ toward God in this life, while disbelievers and wrongdoers show it only in the hereafter.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r3.anchor: وأمعن التدبر لهاذ الملحظ من المراد مجئ خشوع المؤمنين لله في الدنيا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses aflaḥa as winning and prospering, and supports that usage with a line by Labīd.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: فازوا وسعدوا. واستشهد بقول لبيد بن ربيعة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r2.claim: In Arabic, falāḥ can mean success and attaining one's aim; glossing it as victory and happiness is close.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r2.anchor: ومن معاني الفلاح في العربيةك النجاحُ وإدراك البغية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r3.claim: The Qur'an uses the past verb four times, its present form twenty-three times, and its active participle twice, affirming success for faithful groups and denying it of opponents.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r3.anchor: وفي القرآن منه: أفلح، الماضي من الرباعي، أربع مرات، ومضارعع ثلاثاً وعشرين مرة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r4.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes worldly success: attaining the enduring, wealthy, and honorable conditions that make worldly life pleasant.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p341/r4.anchor: وميز "الراغب" بين ضربين منه: الدنيوي وهو الظفر بالسعادات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p127/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p127/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p127/r8.claim: The opening connects to al-Ḥajj’s close, calling believers to worship, do good, establish prayer, give zakāh, and hold fast to God so they may prosper.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p127/r8.anchor: إن آيات النص الأول، هي مفتتح سورة (المؤمنون) ، وارتباطها بآخر السورة قبلها ظاهر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r12.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r12.speaker: ورش عن نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r12.claim: Warsh transfers the hamza’s vowel to the preceding consonant and drops it, both within words and across word boundaries.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r12.anchor: وروى ورش عن نافع أنه كان يلقي حركة الهمزة على اللام التي قبلها مثل ﴿ الأرض ﴾ و ﴿ الآخرة ﴾

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43/r1.speaker: كعب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43/r1.claim: Kaʿb says God created three things with His hand: Adam, the Torah, and the Garden of Eden; when the Garden was told to speak, it said believers have prospered, knowing their honor with God.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ قد أفلح المؤمنون ﴾ قال قال كعب إن الله لم يخلق بيده إلا ثلاثة خلق آدم بيده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.claim: ʿUmar reports that revelation sounded like a buzzing bee near the Prophet’s face; after a pause the Prophet faced the qibla, raised his hands, prayed for generous divine favor, and said that whoever establishes ten verses beginning with this opening will enter the Garden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد القارئ قال: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب يقول: كان إذا نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل وعلي بن المديني وجماعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.claim: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, and others transmit a variant prayer wording that adds a request to be made content, alongside the request for God’s pleasure.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.anchor: ورواه أحمد بن حنبل، وعلي ابن المديني، وجماعة عن عبد الرزاق، وقالوا: "وأعطنا ولا تحرمنا وأرضنا وارض عنا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r1.claim: The particle qad is an emphatic particle.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {قد أفلح المؤمنون} "قد" حرف تأكيد، وقال المحققون: "قد"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r2.speaker: المحققون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r2.claim: Qad brings the past close to the present, indicating that believers have attained success and remain in it; this is more emphatic than stating the verb alone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r2.anchor: وقال المحققون: "قد" تقرب الماضي من الحال، يدل على أن الفلاح قد حصل لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r3.claim: Al-falah means salvation and enduring life; Ibn Abbas explains that those affirming divine oneness are blessed and remain in Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r3.anchor: "والفلاح" النجاة والبقاء، قال ابن عباس: قد سعد المصدقون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the believers who affirm God's oneness attain felicity and remain in Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قد سعد المصدقون بالتوحيد وبقوا في الجنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan; it has 119 verses according to the Basrans and 118 according to the Kufans.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r1.anchor: مكية وهي مائة وتسع عشرة آية عند البصريين وثماني عشرة عند الكوفيين

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r2.claim: Qad affirms an expected outcome, as lamā negates one while indicating its settled occurrence with the past; it brings that past near the present, fitting believers' expectation of God's bounty and their glad tidings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r2.anchor: قد تثبت المتوقع كما أن لما تنفيه وتدل على ثباته إذا دخلت على الماضي

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r3.speaker: ورش عن نافع
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r3.claim: Warsh from Nāfiʿ transfers the hamza's vowel to the dāl and deletes the hamza.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r3.anchor: وقرأ ورش عن نافع { قد أفلح } بإلقاء حركة الهمزة على الدال وحذفها

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r4.claim: Another reading uses plural aflaḥū by dialect or anticipatory subject clarified afterward; other forms use ḍamma instead of wāw or the passive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:1/r4.anchor: وقرىء «أفلحوا» على لغة: أكلوني البراغيث، أو على الإبهام والتفسير، و { أفلح } بالضم اجتزاء بالضمة عن الواو و «أفلح» على البناء للمفعول.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r1.claim: The sūra's purpose is to assign success particularly to believers, as its title plainly indicates.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r1.anchor: مقصودها اختصاص المؤمنين بالفلاح , وتسمها واضح الدلالة على ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r2.claim: Because al-Ḥajj ended by ordering believers' private and public duties, including prayer, zakāt, and divine protection, this sūra opens with qualities that yield good in both lives.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r2.anchor: لما ختمت الحج بناء الذين آمنوا وأمرهم بأمور الدين خاصة وعامة , وختم بالصلاة والزكاة والعصمة به سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r3.claim: The basmala describes God as sovereign over all affairs, al-Raḥmān as giving comprehensive mercy through clear explanation, and al-Raḥīm as singling out whom He wills for faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r3.anchor: الذي له الأمر كله , فلا راد لأمره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r4.claim: Qad signals expectation and brings a completed event near to the present, establishing the anticipated success.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r4.anchor: بحرف التوقع : { قد } وهي نقيضة لما تثبت المتوقع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r5.claim: Aflaha means to win and attain whatever one seeks now, with enduring continuance in good.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r5.anchor: أي فاز وظفر الآن بكل ما يريد , ونال البقاء الدائم في الخير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r6.claim: Calling them believers as a fixed noun signals that those who affirmed faith and acted on the previous sūra's commands deserve this lasting description; the author cites 59:9.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r6.anchor: من أقر بالإيمان وعمل بما أمر به في آخر التي قبلها , استحق الوصف الثابت

DURR-FULL:v6p82/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r1.claim: The sura is Meccan and contains 118 verses.

DURR-FULL:v6p82/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Surat al-Mu'minun was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت بمكة سورة المؤمنين

DURR-FULL:v6p82/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r4.claim: Umar reports that during revelation the Prophet heard a bee-like sound; afterward he prayed for blessing and said ten verses had been revealed whose observance admits one to Paradise, then recited from the opening through the tenth.
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r4.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: كان إذا انزل على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الوحي يسمع عند وجهه كدوي النحل

DURR-FULL:v6p82/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r5.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r5.claim: Aisha says the Prophet's character was the Qur'an; she recited the first ten verses of this sura and said this was his character.
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r5.anchor: عن يزيد بن بابنوس قال: قلنا لعائشة كيف كان خلق رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: كان خلقه القرآن

DURR-FULL:v6p82/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r6.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r6.claim: Anas reports that God created the Garden of Eden with His hand, planted its trees, and asked it to speak; it answered with the opening words of this sura.
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r6.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - خلق الله جنة عدن وغرس أشجارها بيده وقال لها: تكلمي

DURR-FULL:v6p82/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits a similar report that Eden answered God's command with the words that the believers have succeeded.
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r7.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني في السنة وابن مردويه من حديث ابن عباس مثله

DURR-FULL:v6p82/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r8.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r8.claim: Qatada transmits Ka'b's statement that God created only three things with His own hand.
DURR-FULL:v6p82/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {قد أفلح المؤمنون} قال: قال كعب: لم يخلق الله بيده إلا ثلاثة

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r1.claim: God created Adam, the Torah, and the Garden of Eden with His hand, commanded the Garden to speak, and it announced the believers' success because of the honor it contained.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r1.anchor: خلق آدم بيده والتوراة بيده وغرس جنة عدن بيده

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r2.claim: Mujahid says that when God planted Paradise, He looked at it and said, “The believers have succeeded.”
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: لما غرس الله الجنة

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says that when God created Paradise, He declared the believers successful and then revealed this in the Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال: لما خلق الله الجنة

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses the successful believers as those who affirmed God's oneness.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {قد أفلح المؤمنون} يعني: سعد المصدقون

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r5.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r5.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif recited “aflaḥa” with rafʿ, as reported by al-Suyuti.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r5.anchor: عن طلحة بن مصرف أنه كان يقرأ {قد أفلح المؤمنون} برفع أفلح

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r6.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r6.claim: Asim is reported to have recited “aflaḥa” with naṣb.

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains aflaḥa as “they won and became happy,” affirming the word's sense of success and felicity.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله {قد أفلح المؤمنون} قال: فازوا وسعدوا

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r8.speaker: لبيد
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r8.claim: The poet Labid's line using aflaḥa is cited as Arab usage supporting the gloss of success.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r8.anchor: قول لبيد فاعقلي إن كنت ما تعقلي ولقد أفلح من كان عقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r1.claim: The sura is called al-Mu'minun by association with the believers whose success it announces at the opening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r1.anchor: فالأول على اعتبار إضافة السورة إلى المؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r2.claim: Al-Mu'minun can instead quote the exact word that opens the sura and identify it by that wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r2.anchor: والثاني على حكاية لفظ { المؤمنون } الواقع أولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن السائب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r3.claim: Al-Nasa'i reports that Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib saw the Prophet pray at the Ka'ba during the conquest, begin this sura, cough at its mention of Moses or Jesus, and bow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن السائب قال : حضرت رسول الله يوم الفتح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن السائب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r4.claim: Abu Dawud reports Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib saying the Prophet led dawn prayer in Mecca with this sura, coughed at the mention of Moses and Aaron or Moses and Jesus, then cut the recitation short and bowed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r4.anchor: روى أبو داود : ( عن عبد الله بن السائب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r5.speaker: ابن القاسم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r5.claim: Common names include Qad Aflaha and Surat al-Falah; al-Utbiyya cites Ibn al-Qasim relating Malik's grandfather's Uthman-era mushaf and its notation for the sura, in contrast to the reading at 23:85.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r5.anchor: ومما جرى على الألسنة أن يسموها سورة ( قد أفلح )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r6.claim: The sura is Meccan by consensus; the claim that its mention of zakah makes it Medinan is mistaken.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r6.anchor: وهي مكية بالاتفاق . ولا اعتداد بتوقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r1.claim: The repeated relative construction presents each trait as a cause of success because each signals firmly rooted faith; the list need not exhaust piety or every cause of success.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r1.anchor: وبتكريره للإيماء إلى وجه فلاحهم وعلته ، أي أن كل خصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r2.claim: The contrast with condemned people who did not pray, feed the poor, or heed Judgment shows the traits' causal relevance, though an enumeration need not be exhaustive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r2.anchor: كما كانت أضدادها كذلك في قوله تعالى { ما سلككم في سقر قالوا لم نك

BURSEVI:v6p47/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p47/r1.claim: The Meccan surah is counted as 110 verses by Basrans and 118 by Kufans.
BURSEVI:v6p47/r1.anchor: مكية وهي مائة وعشر آيات عند البصريين وثماني عشرة عند الكوفيين

BURSEVI:v6p47/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p47/r2.claim: A hadith says that when God created Eden, it spoke the verse's words; God called it a blessed home of the kings of Paradise, the patient poor.
BURSEVI:v6p47/r2.anchor: فقالت : قد أفلح المؤمنون فقال : طوبى لك ، منزل الملوك

BURSEVI:v6p47/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p47/r3.claim: The past tense signals certain success, and qad confirms the realization of an outcome believers had already expected from God's grace.
BURSEVI:v6p47/r3.anchor: فصيغة الماضي للدلالة على تحقق الدخول في الفلاح وكلمة قد لإفادة ثبوت ما كان متوقع الثبوت

BURSEVI:v6p47/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p47/r4.claim: Success is lasting in Paradise, attaining one's aim, and escaping harm; aflaha means entering that state, like entering glad tidings, or can mean admitting someone into it.
BURSEVI:v6p47/r4.anchor: والفلاح البقاء والفوز بالمراد والنجاة من المكروه والإفلاح الدخول في ذلك كالإبشار

BURSEVI:v6p47/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p47/r5.claim: A passive-voice reading takes aflaha as meaning that believers were admitted into success.
BURSEVI:v6p47/r5.anchor: وقد يجيء متعديا بمعنى الإدخال فيه وعليه قراءة من قرأ على البناء للمفعول

BURSEVI:v6p47/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p47/r6.claim: Basic assent to essential teachings such as oneness, prophethood, resurrection, and recompense does not by itself yield true success; it requires faith with all its conditions.
BURSEVI:v6p47/r6.anchor: لما كان الفلاح الحقيقي لا يحصل بمطلق الإيمان وهو التصديق بما علم ضرورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r1.claim: The believers succeeded by attaining their goal and securing lasting continuance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r1.anchor: أخبر الله تعالى عن فلاح المؤمنين وأنهم نالوا البغية وأحرزوا البقاء الدائم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r2.speaker: كعب الأحبار
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r2.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār reports that when God created the Garden of Eden and asked it to speak, it said that the believers had succeeded.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r2.anchor: وروي عن كعب الأحبار أن الله تعالى لما خلق جنة عدن قال لها تكلمي فقالت قد أفلح المؤمنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r3.claim: Mujāhid reports that after creating and perfecting the Garden, God declared that the believers had succeeded.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r3.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أن الله تعالى لما خلق الجنة وأتقن حسنها قال قد أفلح المؤمنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r4.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r4.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif's reading with ḍamma on ḥāʾ intends afl aḥū, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف «قد أفلح المؤمنون» بضم الحاء يريد قد أفلحوا، وهي قراءة مردودة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r5.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r5.claim: Another reading reported from Ṭalḥa has ḍamma on hamza and kasra on lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r5.anchor: وروي عنه «قد أفلح» بضم الهمزة وكسر اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب عن رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r1.claim: Umar reports the Prophet saying ten verses were revealed: whoever upholds them enters Paradise; he recited from this verse through ten verses. Al-Hakim included it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r1.anchor: روى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لقد أنزلت علينا عشر آيات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r2.claim: Abu Saʿid reports the Prophet describing Paradise's gold and silver wall and its planted tree, which proclaimed that the believers prosper; he said, Blessed is your home, abode of kings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r2.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انه قال إن الله تعالى حاط حائط الجنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r3.claim: Al-Farra says qad may emphasize the believers' success.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r3.anchor: قال الفراء قد هاهنا يجوز أن تكون تأكيدا لفلاح المؤمنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r4.claim: Alternatively, qad brings the past close to the present, as in announcing that the prayer has begun before it actually begins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون تقريبا للماضي من الحال لأن قد تقرب الماضي من الحال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r5.claim: The verse presents success as already attained and still true of the believers now.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r5.anchor: فيكون معنى الآية إن الفلاح قد حصل لهم وإنهم عليه في الحال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب وعكرمة وعاصم الجحدري وطلحة بن مصرف
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r6.claim: These readers pronounce the verb in the passive: the believers have been brought to success.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب وعكرمة وعاصم الجحدري وطلحة بن مصرف قد أفلح بضم الألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains success as attaining lasting permanence in goodness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج ومعنى الآية قد نال المؤمنون البقاء الدائم في الخير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r8.claim: With the passive reading, the meaning is that the believers were made to attain success.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ قد أفلح بضم الألف كان معناه قد أصيروا إلى الفلاح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r1.claim: Umar reports that revelation sounded like bees near the Prophet, who prayed facing the qibla; he then said ten verses had been revealed and whoever upholds them enters Paradise, and recited this passage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r1.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد القاري قال: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب يقول: كان إذا نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r2.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the Umar report munkar, saying only Yunus ibn Sulaym is known to transmit it and that Yunus is unknown; al-Nasa'i also transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r2.anchor: وقال الترمذي: منكر، لا نعرف أحدا رواه غير يونس بن سليم، ويونس لا نعرفه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r3.claim: Aisha says the Prophet's character was the Qur'an and recites this sura through the description of those who guard their prayers as his character.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r3.anchor: عن أبي عمران عن يزيد بن بابنوس قال: قلنا لعائشة: يا أم المؤمنين، كيف كان (6) خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r4.speaker: كعب الأحبار، مجاهد، أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r4.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliya, and others report that God asked the created Garden of Eden to speak and it uttered this verse; Ka'b connects it to its residents' prepared honor, while Abu al-Aliya says God revealed it in His Book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r4.anchor: وقد روي عن كعب الأحبار، ومجاهد، وأبي العالية، وغيرهم: لما خلق الله جنة عدن، وغرسها بيده،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r5.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that God made and planted Paradise from gold and silver bricks; it spoke this verse, and the angels called it a dwelling for kings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p359#4/r5.anchor: فقال أبو بكر البزار: حدثنا محمد بن المثنى، حدثنا المغيرة بن سلمة، حدثنا وهيب، عن الجريري، عن أبي نضرة، عن أبي سعيد قال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r1.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet saying Paradise was built of gold and silver bricks with musk mortar and spoke this verse; al-Bazzar says only Adi ibn al-Fadl raises it to the Prophet and that Adi was not a memorizer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "خلق الله الجنة، لبنة من ذهب ولبنة من فضة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet saying God created Eden with wonders unseen and unheard, then it spoke this verse; al-Tabarani notes Baqiyya is weak when reporting from Hijazis.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r2.anchor: وقال الحافظ أبو القاسم الطبراني: حدثنا أحمد بن علي، حدثنا هشام بن خالد، حدثنا بقية، عن ابن جريج، عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لما خلق الله جنة عدن،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r3.claim: A report raised to the Prophet from Ibn Abbas says God created Eden, placed fruits and rivers in it, and swore that no miser would live beside Him there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس -يرفعه-: "لما خلق الله جنة عدن بيده، ودلى فيها ثمارها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r4.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r4.claim: Anas reports the Prophet describing Eden built from three precious materials with musk mortar and pearl gravel; it spoke this verse, God excluded the miser from its neighborhood, and the Prophet recited 59:9.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r4.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن أبي الدنيا: حدثنا محمد بن المثنى البزار، حدثنا محمد بن زياد الكلبي، حدثنا يعيش بن حسين، عن سعيد بن أبي عروبة، عن قتادة، عن أنس، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r5.claim: The verse means the believers described by these qualities have succeeded, attained happiness, and achieved true flourishing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p460/r5.anchor: فقوله تعالى: {قد أفلح المؤمنون} أي: قد فازوا وسعدوا وحصلوا على الفلاح،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r7.claim: Opening and closing the list of virtues with prayer signals its excellence; a prophetic report likewise says to be upright as possible, calls prayer the best work, and praises maintaining ablution.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r7.anchor: وقد افتتح الله ذكر هذه الصفات الحميدة بالصلاة، واختتمها بالصلاة، فدل على أفضليتها،

JISHUMI:v7p5017/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r1.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r1.claim: Al-Qāḍī says the transmitted view is that Sūrat al-Muʾminūn is Meccan; it has 118 verses in the Kūfan count and 117 in the Baṣran count.
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r1.anchor: قال القاضي: المنقول أنها مكية، وهي مائة وثماني عشرة آية في الكوفي، وسبع في البصري

JISHUMI:v7p5017/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb transmits from the Prophet that reciting the sūra brings angels’ glad tidings of comfort and delight at the time of death.
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r3.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة المؤمنين بشرته الملائكة بالروح

JISHUMI:v7p5017/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r4.speaker: عمر
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r4.claim: In a long report from the Prophet, ʿUmar says that whoever upholds ten verses enters Paradise, then the Prophet recited this sūra’s opening.
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r4.anchor: وعن عمر، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في حديث طويل: لقد أنزل عشر آيات من أقامهن دخل الجنة

JISHUMI:v7p5017/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r5.claim: The sūra opens by detailing the command to worship and do good deeds that closed Sūrat al-Ḥajj; success is attained through them.
JISHUMI:v7p5017/r5.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (الحج) بالأمر بالعبادة وفعل الخيرات افتتح هذه السورة بتفصيل تلك الجملة

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r1.speaker: ورش عن نافع
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r1.claim: Warsh from Nāfiʿ joins قد أفلح without hamza and transfers the hamza’s fatha to the preceding dāl.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r1.anchor: قرأ ورش عن نافع قد افلح بالوصل وترك الهمز

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r2.claim: The other readers keep dāl still and pronounce the initial hamza separately.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بسكون الدال وقطع الألف

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r3.speaker: حمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم وقتيبة عن الكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r3.claim: These readers pause briefly on dāl and separate the hamza; Ḥamza and al-Aʿshā lengthen the pause, while the others do not pause.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r3.anchor: غير أن حمزة وأبا بكر عن عاصم وقتيبة عن الكسائي

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r8.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r8.claim: The common reading has a fatḥa on the initial alif; Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif has a passive form meaning they were cast into the earth.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r8.anchor: قراءة العامة: أفلح بفتح الألف، وعن طلحة بن مصرف: أفلح بمعنى ألقوا في التراب

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r9.claim: قد emphasizes a statement; ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says it brings a past event close to the present, making success already attained and continuing.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r9.anchor: (قد) تأكيد للكلام، قال علي بن عيسى: (قد) تقريب الماضي من الحال

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r10.claim: فلاح means success or lasting life; Arabs call anyone who attains good a successful person.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r10.anchor: والفلاح: الفوز، والفلاح: البقاء، والعرب تقول لكل من أصاب خيرا: مفلح

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r1.claim: The verses reserve Paradise and its reward for believers, refuting Murjiʾites who say a grave sinner attains it.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r1.anchor: يدل أول الآيات أن الجنة والفوز بها للمؤمنين خاصة، فيبطل قول المرجئة أن الفاسق ينالها

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r2.claim: A believer attains the object of his or her desire.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r2.anchor: وتدل أنه لا يؤمن إلا ويظفر ببغيته

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r3.claim: The term believer is a commendatory name and should not be applied to a sinner deserving punishment.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن قولنا: مؤمن من أسماء المدح، ولا يطلق على الفاسق ومن يستحق العقاب

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r4.claim: Another view is that believer is a technical name established by religious law.

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.claim: The listed traits remove ambiguity: whoever has them is a believer, supporting the author’s position.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.anchor: ثم بين تعالى ما أزال كل شبهة، فذكر صفات المؤمن، فدل أن من كانت صفته ما ذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r1.claim: Qad affirms an expected outcome while lammā denies it; it establishes the success believers awaited.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r1.anchor: قد أفلح المؤمنون } نقيضه ( لما ) هي تثبت المتوقع و ( لما ) تنفيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r2.claim: Falāḥ means attaining one’s aim or remaining in goodness; aflaḥa means entering success, and aflaḥahu making someone succeed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r2.anchor: والفلاح : الظفر بالمراد ، وقيل : البقاء في الخير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r3.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r3.claim: Ṭalḥa reads aflaḥa passive, aflaḥū by the ‘akalūnī al-barāghīth’ construction or ellipsis, and aflaḥ with ḍamma instead of wāw, supported by poetry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r3.anchor: وعليه قراءة طلحة بن مصرف : أفلح ، على البناء للمفعول . وعنه : ( أفلحوا )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r4.claim: In language, a believer is one who confirms.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r5.claim: One legal view counts anyone professing the testimonies with heart and tongue aligned as a believer; another reserves the praise for the righteous and pious, excluding sinners.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما : أن كل من نطق بالشهادتين مواطئا قلبه لسانه فهو مؤمن

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r1.claim: One lexical explanation is that aflaha means to be happy or succeed; Labid's verse is cited as evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : معناه قد سعد المؤمنون ومنه قول لبيد :

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r2.claim: A second explanation is lasting: the believers' deeds endure or they abide in Paradise; the call to prayer and poetry support this sense of lasting good.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r2.anchor: أن الفلاح البقاء ومعناه قد بقيت لهم أعمالهم , وقيل : إنه بقاؤهم في الجنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r3.claim: A third explanation is attaining one's aims, illustrated by a poet's line about Mulaʿib al-Rimah attaining falah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنه إدراك المطالب قال الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas defines the successful as those who attain what they seek and escape the evil from which they flee.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المفلحون الذين أدركوا ما طلبوا ونجوا من شر ما منه هربوا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r2.claim: ʿUmar reports that revelation sounded like a bee's drone near the Prophet; the Prophet then prayed for increase, honor, giving, preference, and God's approval, and said whoever upholds these ten verses enters Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r2.anchor: روى عمر بن الخطاب قال كان النبي صل الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه القرآن يسمع عند وجهه دوي كدوي النحل

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r3.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r3.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni reports that Aisha had al-Muʾminun recited through “they guard their prayers,” then said that this was the Prophet's character.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r3.anchor: روى أبو عمران الجوني قال قيل لعائشة ما كان خلق رسول الله صل الله عليه وسلم ؟

MUJAHID:v2p429/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p429/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p429/r1.claim: Mujahid reports that God planted the Gardens of Eden by His hand, closed them when complete, and looks at them each dawn; they say, 'The believers have succeeded.'
MUJAHID:v2p429/r1.anchor: عن جابر عن مجاهد قال أن الله عز وجل غرس جنات عدن بيده فلما تكاملت أغلقت

MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said Firdaws was created and planted by God's hand, incomparable to anything seen or imagined, then commanded to adorn itself twice and speak; it declared that the believers prospered.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r5.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r6.claim: The Prophet's report says Firdaws named the successful as the monotheists of Muhammad's community, who inherit Firdaws eternally.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r6.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r7.claim: The report says Firdaws's gate stays closed until Resurrection, its fragrance and houris are at its entrance, and the Prophet waits at the Pool to turn away unbelievers and recognize his community by ablution's light.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r7.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r8.claim: The Prophet said whoever drinks from his Pool will never thirst again; Muadh called such drinkers fortunate, and the Prophet said a monotheist who believes in the messenger drinks and enters Firdaws.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r8.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r9.claim: The Prophet told Muadh that those who die Muslim were created Muslim in Adam, passed through unbelieving ancestors until they believed in him, and are his brothers, while his contemporaries are his companions.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r9.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

MUQATIL:23:1-6/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:1-6/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:1-6/r1.claim: The believers have prospered, meaning they have become happy; believers here are those who affirm God's oneness.
MUQATIL:23:1-6/r1.anchor: { قد أفلح المؤمنون } [آية: 1] يعنى سعد المؤمنون، يعنى المصدقين بتوحيد الله عز وجل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r1.claim: The particle qad confirms an expected event; believers expected news that success would be secured for them, and the wording confirms it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r1.anchor: قد نقضية لما هى تثبت المتوقع ولما تنفيه وكان المؤمنين يتوقعون مثل هذه البشارة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r2.claim: Success is attaining what one seeks and escaping what one fears.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r2.anchor: والفلاح الظفر بالمطلوب والنجاة من المرهوب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r3.claim: In Arabic, faith means assent, and a believer is one who assents.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r3.anchor: والإيمان فى اللغة التصديق والمؤمن المصدق لغة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r4.claim: In religious usage, a believer is one who voices both testimonies while his heart agrees with his tongue.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r4.anchor: وفى الشرع كل من نطق بالشهادتين موطئا قلبه لسانه فهو مؤمن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r5.claim: A report says God commanded Paradise to speak; it declared believers successful three times and said it is forbidden to every miser and show-off, since showiness nullifies bodily worship and the person has no financial worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#2/r5.anchor: قال عليه السلام خلق الله الجنة فقال لها تكلمى فقالت قد أفلح المؤمنون ثلاثا أنا حرام على كل بخيل مراء

QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r1.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reports from Anas that when God created the Garden of Eden and planted its trees by His hand, He told it to speak and it said, “Successful are the believers.”
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r1.anchor: روى البيهقي من حديث أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن السائب
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r2.claim: Al-Nasa'i reports from Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet prayed facing the Kaaba, began this sura, then coughed and bowed when Moses or Jesus was mentioned; Muslim reports it similarly.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r2.anchor: وروى النسائي عن عبد الله بن السائب قال: حضرت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الفتح فصلى في قبل الكعبة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r3.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Umar that revelation sounded like bees near the Prophet; afterward the Prophet prayed for increase, acceptance, and contentment, then said ten verses had been revealed whose observance admits one to Paradise, and recited them; Ibn al-Arabi authenticated the report.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r3.anchor: وفي الترمذي عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال

QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas glosses “whoever upholds them” as adhering to the ten verses without violating their teachings, like someone carrying out his work.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r4.anchor: وقال النحاس: معنى «من أقامهن» من أقام عليهن ولم يخالف ما فيهن

QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r5.claim: The obligations of ablution and pilgrimage were revealed after these ten verses and were included among what believers must uphold.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r5.anchor: ثم نزل بعد هذه الآيات فرض الوضوء والحج فدخل معهن

QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r6.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r6.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads the hamza with ḍamma as a passive verb, meaning the believers were made successful or preserved in reward and good.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r6.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف «قد أفلح المؤمنون» بضم الألف على الفعل المجهول

QASHANI:23:1-11/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:1-11/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:1-11/r1.claim: The believers who succeed in the greatest victory are those certain of faith.

RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r1.claim: God promises success to those who combine seven qualities; the segment begins explaining those qualities with “the believers.”
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r1.anchor: حكم بحصول الفلاح لمن كان مستجمعا لصفات سبع

RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r2.claim: “Qad” contrasts with “lammā”: it affirms an expected event, here the believers’ anticipated glad tidings that success is firmly theirs.
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r2.anchor: فقد تثبت المتوقع ولما تنفيه ولا شك أن المؤمنين كانوا متوقعين لمثل هذه البشارة

RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r3.claim: Falāḥ means attaining one’s desired end, or remaining in good; aflaha can mean entering success, as abshara means entering glad tidings, or it can be causative, “he made him succeed.”
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r3.anchor: الفلاح الظفر بالراد وقيل البقاء في الخير ، وأفلح دخل في الفلاح كأبشر دخل في البشارة

RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r4.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r4.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif read aflaha in the passive; a further form aflaha is attributed to him either by the “akalūnī al-barāghīth” dialect or by an indefinite verb followed by an explanatory subject.
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r4.anchor: وعليه قراءة طلحة بن مصرف أفلح على البناء للمفعول ، وعنه أفلحوا على لغة أكلوني البراغيث

RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r5.claim: Al-Razi says the explanation of faith has already been given in Surat al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم القول في الإيمان في سورة البقرة

RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r6.claim: A report says the Garden of Eden spoke the opening words after God created it and commanded it to speak.
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r6.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( لما خلق الله تعالى جنة عدن

RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r7.speaker: كعب
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r7.claim: Kaʿb reports that God made Adam, wrote the Torah, and planted the tree Ṭūbā with His hand, then commanded it to speak and it uttered the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r7.anchor: وقال كعب : ( خلق الله آدم بيده وكتب التوراة بيده وغرس شجرة طوبى بيده

RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r8.claim: A report says prayer praises and intercedes for the one who performs it well, but calls down loss on the one who neglects it.
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r8.anchor: إذا أحسن العبد الوضوء وصلى الصلاة لوقتها وحافظ على ركوعها وسجودها ومواقيتها قالت حفظك الله

RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r9.claim: The Garden's speech means that it has been prepared for believers, as in the Qurʾānic personification of heaven and earth saying they came willingly.

RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r10.claim: God's creating the Garden with His hand means He personally undertook its creation rather than delegating it.
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r10.anchor: وأما أنه تعالى خلق الجنة بيده فالمراد تولى خلقها لا أنه وكله إلى غيره

RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r11.claim: Prayer's praise is figurative: prayer consists of movements and stillnesses that cannot literally take form and speak, like saying a benefactor's kindness speaks gratitude.
RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r11.anchor: الصلاة حركات وسكنات ولا يصح عليها أن تتصور

STUDYQURAN:23:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:1/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:1/r1.claim: A tradition says God created Adam, wrote the Torah, and planted Eden with His Hand, then declared that the believers had prospered.
STUDYQURAN:23:1/r1.anchor: and then said, “Truly the believers have prospered” (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:23:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:1/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:1/r2.claim: A separate account says God declared this when He created the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:23:1/r2.anchor: God said this when He created the Garden (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:23:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:1/r3.claim: Aflaha literally means to succeed or thrive and also evokes cultivation; Quranic use distinguishes those who flourish from those who do not, in this life and especially the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:23:1/r3.anchor: “To prosper” has the literal sense of being successful or thriving and is also related to the notion of “cultivation” in an agricultural context

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r1.claim: The name derives from elevation; the named one deserves loftiness, and the Real is true through primordial loftiness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r1.anchor: الاسم اشتقاقه من السمو وللمسمى بهذا الاسم استحقاق العلو ، فالاسم اسم لسموه من القدم ، والحق حق لعلوه بحق القدم

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r2.claim: Knowing Bismillah raises a person’s aspiration and brings the heart knowledge whose cause is unknown to it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r2.anchor: ' بسم الله ' سمت همته ، ومن عرفه وجد بقلبه ما لا يعرف سببه

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r3.claim: Falāḥ means reaching what one seeks and attaining one’s intended goal.

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r4.claim: Faith is truth taking root in the inner self, affirmation permeating the heart’s core, and realization settling in the heart.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r4.anchor: والإيمان انتسام الحق في السريرة ، ومخامرة التصديق خلاصة القلب ، وستمكان التحقيق من تأمور الفؤاد

TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r1.claim: The believers succeed by believing God and His Messenger, accepting the revelation, and doing the acts named in these verses; their reward is lasting Gardens and fulfillment of their hopes with God.
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r1.anchor: الخلود في جنات ربهم وفازوا بطلبتهم لديه

TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r2.speaker: كعب
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r2.claim: Kaʿb says God made Adam, wrote the Torah, and planted Eden by His hand; when told to speak, the Garden said the verse, knowing the honor within it.
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r2.anchor: قال كعب: " لم يخلق الله بيده إلا ثلاثة: خلق آدم بيده، وكتب التوراة بيده، وغرس جنة عدن بيده،

TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says God planted the Garden, looked at it, and said the verse.
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " لما غرس الله تبارك وتعالى الجنة، نظر إليها فقال: {قد أفلح المؤمنون} [المؤمنون: 1] "

TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r4.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says that when God created the Garden He said the verse, which He then revealed in the Qurʾan.
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال: " لما خلق الله الجنة قال: {قد أفلح المؤمنون} [المؤمنون: 1] فأنزل الله به قرآنا "

TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r5.speaker: ميسرة
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r5.claim: Maysara says God created four things by His hand—Adam, the Tablets, the Torah, and Eden—and then said the verse.
TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r5.anchor: عن ميسرة، قال: " لم يخلق الله شيئا بيده غير أربعة أشياء: خلق آدم بيده، وكتب الألواح بيده، والتوراة بيده،

SULAMI:v2p30#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r1.speaker: أحمد بن عاصم الأنطاكي
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r1.claim: The believer’s treasure is his Lord, his aversion is this world, his beloved is the hereafter, his provision is piety, and his gathering is remembrance.
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r1.anchor: قال أحمد بن عاصم الأنطاكي : المؤمن من تكون بضاعته مولاه

SULAMI:v2p30#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r2.claim: Success is reaching the highest station of nearness and happiness through affirming God’s promise.
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمة الله عليه في هذه الآية : وصل إلى المحل الأعلى والقربة

SULAMI:v2p30#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r3.claim: A believer is trustworthy with heart, spirit, secret, and limbs; faith entails integrity outwardly and inwardly.
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : المؤمن يكون أمينا على قلبه ، أمينا على روحه

SULAMI:v2p30#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r4.claim: A believer is safe for himself and others, welcomes and comforts people, and his company is solace for believers, mercy for seekers, and counsel for the pious.
SULAMI:v2p30#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : المؤمن يكون من نفسه في أمن ، والخلق منه في أمن

TABATABAI:23:1/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1/r1.claim: The Meccan sura calls people to believe in God and the Last Day, contrasts believers’ fine servitude with disbelievers’ vices, then gives glad tidings and warnings including the annihilation of denying peoples from Noah through Jesus.
TABATABAI:23:1/r1.anchor: دعوة إلى الإيمان بالله واليوم الآخر وتمييز المؤمنين من الكفار بذكر ما لهؤلاء من جميل صفات العبودية

TABATABAI:23:1/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1/r2.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:23:1/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says falh means a cleft or splitting, illustrated by iron splitting iron; falah then means success and attainment of a goal.
TABATABAI:23:1/r2.anchor: قال الراغب الفلح - بالفتح فالسكون - الشق

TABATABAI:23:1/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1/r3.claim: Success has worldly and afterlife forms: worldly happiness includes long life, wealth, and honor; the afterlife brings permanence, freedom from poverty, freedom from disgrace, and knowledge without ignorance.
TABATABAI:23:1/r3.anchor: فالدنيوي الظفر بالسعادات التي تطيب بها الحياة الدنيا

TABATABAI:23:1/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1/r4.claim: Calling attainment falah evokes splitting through the obstacle and uncovering the face of one’s desired goal.
TABATABAI:23:1/r4.anchor: فتسمية الظفر بالسعادة فلاحا بعناية أن فيه شقا للمانع وكشفا عن وجه المطلوب

TABATABAI:23:1/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1/r5.claim: Iman is affirming something while committing to its implications; Qur’anic faith in God affirms His oneness, messengers, the Last Day, and their message, with general obedience.
TABATABAI:23:1/r5.anchor: والإيمان هو الإذعان والتصديق بشيء بالالتزام بلوازمه

TABATABAI:23:1/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1/r6.claim: The Qur’an regularly pairs believers’ praise and reward with righteous action, as in its promise of a good life to anyone who acts righteously while believing and its praise of believers who do good works.
TABATABAI:23:1/r6.anchor: ولذا نجد القرآن كلما ذكر المؤمنين بوصف جميل أو أجر جزيل شفع الإيمان بالعمل الصالح كقوله من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن

TABATABAI:23:1/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1/r7.claim: Belief is not mere mental assent without commitment: faith includes settled assurance and adherence to implications, whereas knowledge can coexist with failure to abandon harmful or shameful habits.
TABATABAI:23:1/r7.anchor: وليس مجرد الاعتقاد بشيء إيمانا به حتى مع عدم الالتزام بلوازمه وآثاره فإن الإيمان علم بالشيء مع السكون والاطمئنان إليه

TABATABAI:23:2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:2/r1.claim: Faith may coexist with disobedience to some of its implications under psychological resistance, but it cannot be wholly detached from its requirements.
TABATABAI:23:2/r1.anchor: والإيمان وإن جاز أن يجتمع مع العصيان عن بعض لوازمه في الجملة لصارف من الصوارف النفسانية

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.claim: The traits in the opening passage show faith as living and active, producing its effects so that the believer reaches the intended end, success.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية إلى تمام ثماني آيات تذكر من أوصاف المؤمنين ما يلازم كون وصف الإيمان حيا فعالا

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r4.claim: Religion is a social way of life based on beliefs about the universe and humanity; social customs and laws therefore vary with those beliefs.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r4.anchor: فالدين سنة عملية مبنية على الاعتقاد في أمر الكون والإنسان بما أنه جزء من أجزائه

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r5.claim: Those who believe in a Lord as the universe's source and return, and in enduring human life, shape conduct toward lasting happiness in the afterlife.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r5.anchor: فمن يثبت للكون ربا يبتدئ منه وسيعود إليه وللإنسان حياة باقية لا تبطل بموت ولا فناء

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r6.claim: Those who affirm deities governing through favor and displeasure but no return to God organize life to please them and gain worldly goods and desires.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r6.anchor: ومن يثبت له إلها أو آلهة تدبر الأمر بالرضا والسخط من غير معاد إليه يعيش عيشة نظمها على أساس التقرب من الآلهة

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r7.claim: Materialists, who disregard lordship and deny lasting human life, base social laws on enjoyment of the finite life ending at death.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r7.anchor: ومن لا يهتم بأمر الربوبية ولا يرى للإنسان حياة خالدة كالماديين ومن يحذو حذوهم يبني سنة الحياة

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r8.claim: Theoretical knowledge about God and humanity does not itself direct action; faith is practical knowledge or judgment that one must follow what that knowledge entails.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r8.anchor: فإن العلم النظري لا يستتبع بنفسه عملا وإن توقف عليه العمل بل هو العلم بوجوب الجري على ما يقتضيه هذا النظر

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r9.claim: Religious preaching addresses practical commitment to true belief in God, messengers, the Last Day, and revelation, including worship and conduct for happiness in both lives.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r9.anchor: فالإيمان الذي يتعلق به الدعوة هو الالتزام بما يقتضيه الاعتقاد الحق في الله سبحانه ورسله واليوم الآخر

TABRISI:23:1-3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:1-3/r6.claim: Those who believe in God’s oneness and His messengers have won God’s reward.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r6.anchor: أي فاز بثواب الله الذين صدقوا بالله وبوحدانيته وبرسله

TABRISI:23:1-3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:23:1-3/r7.claim: One explanation gives aflaḥ the sense of remaining: the believers’ good deeds have endured.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r7.anchor: وقيل: معنى أفلح بقي أي قد بقيت أعمالهم الصالحة

TABRISI:23:1-3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:23:1-3/r8.claim: Another explanation gives aflaḥ the sense of becoming happy or prosperous; Labid’s line is cited as evidence.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r8.anchor: وقيل: معناه قد سعد. قال لبيد: ولقد أفلح من كان عقل

TABRISI:23:1-3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r9.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:23:1-3/r9.claim: Al-Farraʾ says qad confirms success or brings a past event near the present, as when the prayer call precedes prayer.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r9.anchor: قال الفراء: يجوز أن يكون قد ههنا لتأكيد الفلاح للمؤمنين

THALABI:v7p37#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p37#3/r1.claim: Qad emphasizes the statement and brings a past event close to the present: believers’ success has happened and continues, a stronger description than simply mentioning success.
THALABI:v7p37#3/r1.anchor: قد حرف تأكيد، وقال المحققون: معنى قد تقريب بالماضي من الحال، فدل على أن فلاحهم قد حصل وهم عليه في الحال

THALABI:v7p37#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p37#3/r2.claim: Falāḥ means success and lasting continuance.

THALABI:v7p37#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p37#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Garden of Eden spoke when God commanded it, saying ‘the believers have succeeded’ three times and barring misers and show-offs.
THALABI:v7p37#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لما خلق الله سبحانه جنة عدن خلق فيها ما لا عين رأت

THALABI:v7p37#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r4.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
THALABI:v7p37#3/r4.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads the verb passively: believers were made successful in their reward.
THALABI:v7p37#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف: قد أفلح المؤمنون على المجهول، أي أبقوا في الثواب.

THALABI:v7p41/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p41/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v7p41/r1.claim: Umar reports that revelation sounded like bees; after praying for increase, honor, and favor, the Prophet said whoever establishes the ten revealed verses enters Paradise and recited the opening ten verses of this sura.
THALABI:v7p41/r1.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد القاري قال: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله عنه يقول: كان إذا نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي يسمع عند وجهه كدوي النحل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r1.claim: Al-Layth says قد is a particle that affirms an occurrence, adding emphasis to the truth of the statement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r1.anchor: قال الليث: (قد) حرف يوجب به الشيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r2.speaker: النحويون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r2.claim: Grammarians say قد can bring a past verb close to the present, as in قد قامت الصلاة.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r2.anchor: وقال النحويون (¬6): قد تقرب الماضي من الحال حتى تلحقه بحكمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r3.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r3.claim: The cited poem, أم صبي قد حبا أو دارج, likewise uses قد with a past form as a current state: crawling or toddling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا قول الشاعر: أم صبي قد حبا أو دارج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r4.claim: Al-Farra says a past verb used as a circumstantial clause requires قد, stated or understood, as in 4:90.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: الحال (¬2) في الفعل الماضي لا يكون إلا بإضمار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r5.claim: Here قد may emphasize the believers’ success or bring the past close to the present: their success has been attained and remains theirs now.
