WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r5.anchor: و (قد) هاهنا يجوز أن تكون تأكيدا لفلاح المؤمنين، ويجوز أن تكون تقريبا للماضي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the believers have attained felicity and remain in Paradise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: يريد قد سعد المصدقون وبقوا في الجنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq explains their success as attaining everlasting life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r7.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي قد نالوا البقاء الدائم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r8.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r8.claim: Humayd reports from Anas that the Prophet said God created and planted the Garden of Eden, told it to speak, and it said the believers had succeeded; the source gives no grading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r8.anchor: وروى (¬3) حميد، عن أنس، أن رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r9.speaker: كعب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r9.claim: A report from Ka‘b likewise says God planted Eden with His hand and commanded it to speak, whereupon it declared the believers successful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r9.anchor: وهذا كما يروى عن كعب أنه قال: إن الله غرس جنة عدن بيده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r1.claim: The believers have prospered: they attain happiness and lasting life in Paradise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r1.anchor: سعد المصدقون، ونالوا البقاء في الجنة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r1.claim: The believers have prospered by becoming happy; the happy ones are the people of Paradise.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r1.anchor: قد سعد المؤمنون، والسعداء أهل الجنة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r2.speaker: كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r2.claim: Ka'b says God made only Adam, the Torah, and Paradise with His hand; He told Paradise to speak, and it spoke this verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r2.anchor: أن كعبا قال: لم يخلق الله بيده إلا ثلاثة، خلق آدم بيده، وكتب التوراة بيده

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r3.speaker: المعلى بن هلال
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r3.claim: Al-Mu'alla reports that God built Paradise with gold and silver bricks and musk mortar, filled it, spoke this verse, then closed it so no angel or prophet knows what is inside; the dawn's coolness and scent escape through its door.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r3.anchor: المعلى بن هلال ذكره بإسناد قال: إن الله خلق الجنة بيده، فجعل لبنة ذهب، ولبنة فضة

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r1.claim: Falah means attaining one's desired goal or triumph; it is also defined as abiding in goodness.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r1.anchor: “Felah”, murâda zafer bulmaktır. Hayırda bekā diye de târif edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r2.claim: Iflah can mean causing someone to attain success or entering into success; the Qur'an generally uses it in the latter sense.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r2.anchor: “İflâh”, felâha nâil kılmak mânasına geldiği gibi felâha girmek, yani bizim tâbirimizle felâh bulmak mânasına da gelir

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r3.claim: God promises certain success to people who gather seven qualities; faith is the first, discussed at length in al-Baqara.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r3.anchor: yedi sıfatı câmi‘olan kimseler için felâhın muhakkak husûlünü tebşir buyurmaktadır ki bu yedi sıfattan evvelkisi imandır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r1.claim: The first eleven verses summarize essential worship and moral principles and set out the life expected of anyone professing faith or Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r1.anchor: Bu bölümdeki on bir âyette İslâm’ın ibadet ve ahlâk alanlarında vazgeçilmez saydığı ilkelerin yanı sıra mümin kavramının içeriği özetlenmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r2.claim: The success promised here primarily means salvation and well-being in the afterlife, given the sūra’s later rejection of afterlife-deniers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r2.anchor: buradaki “kurtuluş”un öncelikle âhiret kurtuluşu ve esenliği olduğu anlaşılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r3.speaker: hadis
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r3.claim: A cited hadith says whoever fulfills these verses’ requirements will enter Paradise, supporting the afterlife sense of success.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r3.anchor: Kim bu âyetlerin gereğini yaparsa cennete girecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r4.claim: Right belief and good conduct also provide a recipe for happiness and well-being in this world, as transmitted evidence and human experience show.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:1/r4.anchor: bu âyetlerin dünyadaki kurtuluşun bir reçetesini verdiği de muhakkaktır

BURHAN:v1p185/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p185/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v1p185/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī highlights the contrast between al-Muʾminūn’s opening, “the believers have succeeded,” and its ending, “the disbelievers do not succeed.”
BURHAN:v1p185/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشرى وقد جعل الله فاتحة سورة المؤمنين ﴿ قد أفلح المؤمنون ﴾ وأورد فى خاتمتها

BURHAN:v4p305/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p305/r1.claim: Qad may precede a perfect verb or an imperfect verb, provided the imperfect has no jussive, subjunctive, or future particle before it.
BURHAN:v4p305/r1.anchor: تدخل على الماضي المتصرف وعلى المضارع بشرط تجرده عن الجازم والناصب وحرف التنفيس

BURHAN:v4p305/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p305/r2.claim: The particle qad has five uses: expectation, approximation, diminution, abundance, and confirmation.
BURHAN:v4p305/r2.anchor: وتأتي لخمس معان التوقع والتقريب والتقليل والتكثير والتحقيق

BURHAN:v4p305/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r3.speaker: الخليل
BURHAN:v4p305/r3.claim: Al-Khalīl explains qad in “prayer has been established” as addressing a congregation waiting for the prayer to begin; likewise, “he has sat” can announce awaited good.
BURHAN:v4p305/r3.anchor: وقال الخليل إن قولك قد قعد كلام لقول ينتظرون الخير ومنه قول المؤذن قد قامت الصلاة لأن الجماعة منتظرون

BURHAN:v4p305/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r4.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p305/r4.claim: Ibn Mālik’s wording suggests that qad with a perfect verb brings the event near to the present rather than marking expectation; al-Zarkashī allows both senses.
BURHAN:v4p305/r4.anchor: وظاهر كلام ابن مالك في تسهيله

BURHAN:v4p305/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p305/r5.claim: With a perfect verb, expectation can mean that the event was anticipated and has now occurred; qad therefore suits matters awaited by the hearers.
BURHAN:v4p305/r5.anchor: ولكن معنى التوقع فيه إن قد تدل على أنه كان متوقعا منتظرا ثم صار ماضيا ولذلك تستعمل في الأشياء المترقبة

BURHAN:v4p305/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p305/r6.claim: Beginning with qad is appropriate when answering an expectation: the audience awaited knowledge of its standing before God, and the woman awaited an answer to her prayer.
BURHAN:v4p305/r6.anchor: واعلم أنه ليس من الوجه الابتداء بها إلا أن تكون جوابا لمتوقع

BURHAN:v4p305/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p305/r7.claim: With a perfect verb, qad marks approximation to the present and is required when that verb occurs as a circumstantial clause.
BURHAN:v4p305/r7.anchor: وأما التقريب فإنها ترد للدلالة عليه مع الماضي فقد فتدخل لتقريبه من الحال ولذلك تلزم قد مع الماضي إذا وقع حالا

BURHAN:v4p305/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r8.speaker: المبرد والفراء
BURHAN:v4p305/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Farrāʾ posit an implicit qad before “our goods have been returned to us”; others reject supplying an omitted particle.

BURHAN:v4p305/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r9.speaker: ابن عصفور
BURHAN:v4p305/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr says an affirmative perfect in an oath answer takes qad and the lām when near the present, but only the lām when remote.
BURHAN:v4p305/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عصفور إن جواب القسم بالماضي المتصرف المثبت إن كان قريبا من زمن الحال دخلت عليه قد واللام

BURHAN:v4p305/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p305/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p305/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s discussion of “We sent Noah” in an oath answer reads qad with the perfect as signaling expectation.
BURHAN:v4p305/r10.anchor: وكلام الزمخشري يدل على أن قد مع الماضي في جواب القسم للتوقع

NAHHAS:v3p109/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p109/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p109/r1.claim: In the softened reading of قد أفلح, the hamza’s vowel moves to the preceding sukūn-bearing dāl, then the hamza drops to avoid adjacent sukūns.
NAHHAS:v3p109/r1.anchor: ومن قرأ ( قد أفلح ) ألقى حركة الهمزة على الدال وحذف الهمزة لأن الدال كانت ساكنة وإذا خففت الهمزة

ITQAN:v2p487/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p487/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p487/r1.claim: قد enters affirmative, finite, ungoverned verbs; with a past verb it emphasizes realization and can bring a distant past closer to the present.
ITQAN:v2p487/r1.anchor: التحقيق مع الماضي نحو ﴿ قد أفلح المؤمنون ﴾ ﴿ قد أفلح من زكاها ﴾

ITQAN:v1p229#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r2.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r2.claim: Ibn al-Jazari prefers examples such as the paired directions, prophets, prayer and almsgiving, and the story endings in al-Muʾminun for necessity-licensed stopping.
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن الجزري والأحسن تمثيله بنحو ﴿ قبل المشرق والمغرب ﴾ وبنحو ﴿ النبيين ﴾

ITQAN:v1p123/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p123/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p123/r1.claim: The Qurʾan was revealed in batches according to need—five, ten, more, or fewer verses; examples include the Ifk passage, the opening of al-Muʾminun, a single phrase, and a later part of a verse.
ITQAN:v1p123/r1.anchor: الذي استقرئ من الأحاديث الصحيحة وغيرها أن القرآن كان ينزل بحسب الحاجة خمس آيات وعشرا وأكثر وأقل وقد صح نزول العشر آيات في قصة الإفك جملة

ITQAN:v3p296/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p296/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p296/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari notes the contrast between al-Mu'minun's opening, “The believers have succeeded,” and its close, “The disbelievers do not succeed”; al-Kirmani gives the same observation.
ITQAN:v3p296/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري وقد جعل الله فاتحة سورة

ITQAN:v2p350/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p350/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p350/r5.claim: Aflaha means succeeded and prospered; Labid ibn Rabiʿa's line uses the same word as evidence.
ITQAN:v2p350/r5.anchor: قال فازوا وسعدوا قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت قول لبيد بن ربيعة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.claim: Umar describes revelation’s bee-like sound and the Prophet’s supplication, then reports that whoever upholds the first ten verses of al-Muʾminun enters Paradise.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.anchor: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - يقول

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r9.claim: Al-Muminun contrasts its opening declaration that believers succeed with its closing declaration that unbelievers do not succeed.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r9.anchor: جعل فاتحة السورة: {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ المؤمنون} [المؤمنون: 1] وأورد في خاتمتها: {إِنَّهُ لاَ يُفْلِحُ الكافرون}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r1.claim: The earlier promise of hoped-for success is fulfilled in قد أفلح: قد marks confirmation, expectation, and the quick realization of what believers hoped for.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r1.anchor: لقد ابتدأ بالصفة التي تستدعي الفلاح، ولا فلاح من دونها وهي الإيمان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r2.speaker: البحر المحيط
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r2.claim: Al-Bahr al-Muhit links the end of al-Hajj, which urges believers to worship so they may succeed, with the opening report that believers have succeeded.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r2.anchor: جاء في (البحر المحيط) في هذه السورة: "ومناسبتها لآخر السورة قبلها ظاهر، لأنه تعالى خاطب المؤمنين بقوله: {ياأيها الذين آمَنُواْ اركعوا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r3.claim: Faith is the necessary first condition of success; the sūra's opening success of believers is balanced by its closing statement that disbelievers do not succeed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r3.anchor: فقد قال في أول السورة: {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ المؤمنون} ، وقال في خاتمتها: {إِنَّهُ لاَ يُفْلِحُ الكافرون} .

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.claim: The commands to bow, prostrate, worship, do good, establish prayer and give zakat match the opening of al-Muʾminun and its listed believer qualities.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.anchor: فأنت ترى من الأمر بالركوع والسجود وعبادة الله، وفعل الخير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r2.claim: Al-Hajj makes success a hoped-for result of the commands, whereas al-Muʾminun declares that success has occurred after the believers obeyed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r2.anchor: فقد أمرهم بالركوع والسجود، ليرجى لهم الفلاح، وهنا تحقق الفلاح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r3.claim: The verbal form in the address describes becoming believers, while the nominal المؤمنون presents their response as a settled quality.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r3.anchor: فناداهم بالصيغة الفعلية الدالة على الحدوث، فاستجابوا واتصفوا بذلك على وجه الثبات

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r1.claim: A person's success before God depends on faith rooted deeply in the heart; outward profession alone carries no weight.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r1.anchor: To God, success of a person is entirely based on the faith that should deeply penetrate into the heart of a person.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.claim: The next sūrah, al-Nūr, supplements this one: faith illuminating the inner self brightens individual and collective life, while its absence darkens both.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.anchor: Details of all these points will be found in the next sūrah: Sūrah al-Nūr which is the supplement of this sūrah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.claim: Islahi summarizes the earlier passage as a progression from inward faith through prayer, zakāh, restraint, fidelity, and guarded prayer to lasting success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.anchor: on them depends the success of the believers.

ITQAN:v1p115/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p115/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
ITQAN:v1p115/r2.claim: Abu Umama reports that God revealed to Abraham passages also revealed to Muhammad, from several sūras; only Abraham and Muhammad fulfilled these stated qualities.
ITQAN:v1p115/r2.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم من طريق القاسم عن أبي أمامة قال أنزل الله على إبراهيم مما أنزل على محمد
